external_entities.name: readers
external_entities.description: People who access the public site and fetch images, stylesheets and downloads.

external_entities.name: admin

external_entities.source_excerpt: Readers fetch those from the CDN over HTTP.

processes.name: web server
processes.description: The web server for the public content site, which runs the CMS and serves the site.
processes.source_excerpt: The web server runs the CMS and keeps pages, accounts and comments in a MySQL database on the same hosted network.

data_flows.name: fetch assets

data_flows.source_excerpt: Readers fetch those from the CDN over HTTP.

data_flows.name: maintain content
data_flows.description: The web server keeps pages, accounts and comments in the database.

data_flows.name: publish assets
data_flows.description: The web server pushes newly published assets to the CDN's bucket.

data_flows.name: maintain database
data_flows.description: The admin directly maintains the database through an unsecured MySQL connection.

data_flows.notes: There is no jump host, and the admin connects from an unspecified location.

assumptions.assumption: The web server is reachable from the internet because it serves the public site.
assumptions.basis: The source calls it the "Public site" and says readers hit the web server over HTTPS.

assumptions.assumption: The web server presents a web interface.
assumptions.basis: The source describes it as the web server for the public site.

assumptions.assumption: The CMS presents a web interface.
assumptions.basis: The CMS is the application run by the web server for the public site.

assumptions.assumption: The web server both reads and writes pages, accounts and comments because it keeps them in the database.
assumptions.basis: The source says the web server "keeps pages, accounts and comments" in the database.

assumptions.assumption: The admin's direct database maintenance involves both reading and writing.
assumptions.basis: The source says the admin "maintains the database directly".
